Senses.PreferredTarget: the white ox in the open ground
AlternateTargets: the great white ox on open ground
the white ox out in the open
Senses.Explanation: The white ox standing out on the bare open ground (露地). In the records it appears in the ox-herding image beside “the water buffalo” (水牯牛): after the buffalo has been watched and reined back from the crops for years, 'it now turns into the white ox in the open ground' (如今變作箇露地白牛) — it stands naked in plain sight, needs no more herding, and can be let loose without wandering off (躶躶地放他不肯去). These passages call it “the white ox in the open” (露地白牛), say that it has changed after years of tending, and record that when released it does not go away. One corpus text glosses the image element by element: the (五冠山瑞雲寺和尚) chapter of (祖堂集) (B25n0144) has (所言露地白牛者)，(露地是所證之法故)，(即遮那是也)。(白牛是能證之人故)，(即是文殊是也), continuing (白牛運轉)，(不住此處故)，(即普賢是也) — 'the open ground is what is realized… the white ox is the person who realizes… the ox's moving on, not staying in this place…'. The image is drawn from the Lotus Sutra’s burning-house passage (the great white-ox cart the father gives out on the open ground; 白牛車: 99 hits in 68 allowlist texts), and Chan writers cite that pedigree explicitly ('華嚴論主深歎法華經中露地白牛'). Its classic Chan locus is the Guiyang ox-herding line credited to Changqing Da'an at Guishan's assembly — the very 'watch one water-buffalo... now it becomes the white ox in the open' line that floats between Da'an and Nanquan in the sources (flagged in the 水牯牛 pilot). It is also a stock test-question in its own right — (如何是露地白牛) 'What is the white ox in the open?' occurs 59 times in 30 allowlist texts, drawing answers as varied as Deshan's lowing (吽)！(吽)！ 'Moo! Moo!', the herding-shout (叱叱) (given by both 溈山 and 投子 in C078n1720), (針劄不入) 'a needle can't prick in' (D48n8939), (破盆子) 'a broken basin' and (月下不用色) (both D48n8939). In (傳燈玉英集) (B14n0082, 𣵠州杏山鑒洪禪師 section) Linji himself puts the question — (臨濟問如何是露地白牛師曰吽濟曰啞却杏山口師曰老兄作麼生濟曰遮畜生) 'Linji asked: what is the white ox in the open? The master [Xingshan] said: Moo. Linji said: mute Xingshan's mouth! The master said: elder brother, how then? Linji said: this beast!' — so the record carries the lowing answer under (杏山鑒洪) questioned by Linji (B14n0082) and, separately, under (德山鑑禪師) questioned by a monk (X67n1299); the two attributions should not be merged. Finally it is the subject of Beichan Zhixian's much-quoted year-end talk, 'cooking the white ox in the open to see out the year' (烹露地白牛分歲) — the cooking phrase (烹露地白牛) alone recurs 83 times across 64 allowlist texts. A shortened (露地牛) also circulates (53 hits, 43 texts), notably in the verse line (玉角霜毛露地牛) 'jade horns, frost-white coat — the ox in the open', headed (洞山聰頌云) in X67n1299.
Senses.Note: Cross-reference “water buffalo” (水牯牛; entry t_36aa29eb1287): the texts place “the white ox in the open” (露地白牛) after the years of watching and reining in the buffalo. 341 raw occurrences across 153 allowlist texts. Grep-verified deployment split (Zen allowlist): test-question (如何是露地白牛) 79 hits / 34 texts; year-end cooking phrase (烹露地白牛) 83 / 64; short form (露地牛) 49 / 40 (verse line 玉角霜毛露地牛 4 / 3); Lotus cart (白牛車) 93 / 65 (大白牛車 6 / 6). Whose image? No single owner — Lotus-Sutra-derived, with the Guiyang ox-herding line (Da'an, floating to Nanquan) as its Chan locus classicus; strongly multi-source.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只看一頭水牯牛。若落路入草便牽出。若犯人苗稼即鞭撻調伏。既久可憐生受人言語。如今變作箇露地白牛常在面前。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The ox-herding line: the tamed buffalo 'now turns into the white ox in the open.' Attributed to Da'an here but to 'Nanquan said' at T51n2076 0464c12 — a floating attribution (see 水牯牛 pilot).

Occurrences.Kwic: 三十年看一頭水牯牛，若犯人苗稼，摘鼻拽回。如今變成露地白牛，躶躶地放他不肯去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yang Jie (楊傑/提刑) quoting 'Nanquan said' (不見南泉道 at lb 0890b05, immediately before this line) — the Nanquan side of the floating Da'an/Nanquan attribution; a parallel of the Nanquan-version passage at T51n2076 0464c12, not an independent third rendition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山道：露地白牛，牧人懶放。南泉却自小牧水牯牛，且道他意作麼生？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Credited to Dongshan (洞山道) in this verse-commentary; pairs the white ox (needs no herding) against Nanquan's water-buffalo.

Occurrences.Kwic: 德山鑑禪師。僧問：如何是露地白牛？師云：吽！吽！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (露地白牛) used as a stock test-question; Deshan answers with the ox's own lowing ('Moo! Moo!').

Occurrences.Kwic: 北禪賢大師除夕示眾：『年窮歲盡，無可與諸人分歲，老僧烹一頭露地白牛，炊黍米飯，煮野菜根，燒榾柮火，大家喫了
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 不會禪師語錄, year-end informal address raising Beichan Xian's year-end address. Beichan Xian is the exact speaker of the stored quotation: the text introduces 北禪賢大師除夕示眾 and quotes him saying that he will cook one open-ground white ox, rice, and wild-vegetable roots for everyone to eat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 華嚴論主深歎法華經中露地白牛，及以是法住法位，世間相常住。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Puan Yinsu (普菴印肅禪師語錄), Puan Yinsu's extended instruction. Puan Yinsu is the exact narrator who says that Li Tongxuan, the Huayan Treatise Lord, deeply praised the open-ground white ox in the Lotus Sutra; Li is the person discussed, not the speaker of this turn.
